To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the RHA I rat model for schizophrenia relevant behaviors and cognition is confirmed by the present results, which add further face validity to this animal model, and (2) the unexpected volumetric results might be related to the particularly long isolation rearing period used here.
1. Social isolation reared rats show schizophrenia relevant behavioral profiles, 2. These behavioral profiles are accompanied by volumetric changes in mPFC dSt and HPC.
the RHA rats display the common social isolation syndrome, characterized by PPI deficits, hyperactivity and increased anxiety responses, when compared to RLA rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neurobiological substrates of the behavioral alterations induced by social isolation rearing in Roman rats.
the study of the neuroanatomically correlates of behavioral and cognitive alterations in an animal model of schizophrenia, with particular emphasis on the role of the prefrontal cortex.
the effects of long term social isolation on the behavioral profiles and brain morphology of two rat strains with opposite behavioral profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the isolation rearing treatment in RHA I rats induces behavioral and cognitive profiles relevant for schizophrenia and that the long term isolation rearing period might have a compensatory role on brain volume.

the RHA I strain is not a good model for schizophrenia relevant cognitive and behavioral profiles, and the RHA I x isolation interaction is not a good animal model for schizophrenia, but the RHA x isolation interaction might be.

the isolation rearing in RHA I rats is a valid model for the schizophrenia related cognitive and behavioral deficits but the long lasting nature of the rearing procedure does not seem to be able to induce schizophrenia relevant brain volumetric alterations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the isolation rearing paradigm is a powerful tool for studying schizophrenia, as it is able to induce a behavioral syndrome that is very similar to the one observed in schizophrenic patients, and that it is also able to induce volumetric changes in the brain regions that are most affected in the disease, such as mPFC, dSt and HPC.

, after 28 weeks of isolation rearing, RHA I rats display a behavioral phenotype relevant for schizophrenia, while RLA I rats do not show a significant behavioral phenotype, but both strains display an increase in volume in mPFC.
long lasting isolation reared rats, despite the robust behavioral and cognitive alterations, do not display the typical brain volume changes associated to the isolation rearing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RHA I rat model of schizophrenia relevant behaviors and cognitive impairments, can be further validated by the use of a long lasting isolation reared paradigm.

the RHA I rat is a good model for schizophrenia relevant behaviors, and that the long-lasting social isolation rearing treatment might have a different impact on brain development and function when compared to the shorter treatments.

the RHA I rat is a valid model of schizophrenia relevant behavioral and attentional and memory deficits and that the RHA RLA strain differences are a valid model of genetic schizophrenia vulnerability.
